title: from_smtp_message: datetime conversion has untested offset edge case
description: The received_at conversion in Email::from_smtp_message does string surgery: if the string contains 'T' but does not end with 'Z', it appends 'Z'. This correctly handles a future schema change to store ISO-8601 UTC datetimes, but it silently corrupts any value that contains a non-UTC offset (e.g. '2024-01-01T12:00:00+05:30' becomes '2024-01-01T12:00:00+05:30Z', which is malformed RFC 3339). The fix is either (a) store received_at in the schema as strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now') so the format contract is enforced at write time and no branch is needed, or (b) parse with chrono and re-emit, rather than ad-hoc string surgery. There are also zero unit tests for from_smtp_message's datetime path; the test coverage gap means the edge case is invisible.
